about: SMT is a Surat-based Class III medical device maker focused on vascular intervention (drug-eluting stents, PTCA balloons) and structural heart products (TAVI valves, occluders). It has two plants in India and one in Thailand, and sold in 77 countries in FY26. It claims nearly 25% share of India's DES volume. Europe is its largest market at 38.66% of FY26 revenue.

objects.purpose: Offer for Sale by Selling Shareholders (company receives no proceeds); listing benefits

promoters.background: Company was founded in 2001 by Dhirajlal Kotadia; Bhargav Kotadia is Managing Director and CEO. Samara Capital (29.61%), NHPEA Sparkle (15.24%) and Kotak Pre-IPO Fund (5.98%) are other large shareholders and sellers in the OFS.

concentration.note: Top 10 distributors were 15.71% of FY26 revenue (26.34% in FY24); top distributor 3.01%; no single customer above 10%. Top 10 countries were 78.76% of FY26 revenue.

litigation_note: Against the Company: 2 criminal, 98 tax and 5 regulatory proceedings with quantifiable amount Rs 131.97 crore; against Directors Rs 24.85 crore (4 criminal, 4 tax); against Promoters Rs 6.10 crore (4 tax); against subsidiaries Rs 7.00 crore. No material civil litigation.
strengths: Nearly 25% share of India's drug-eluting stent volume in FY26 and top-five DES player in Germany, Spain, Poland and Brazil, per the F&S industry report.
Diversified revenue: India 26%, Europe 39% and rest of world 35% in FY26, sold in 77 countries.
Broad Class III portfolio across stents, balloons, TAVI valves and occluders, backed by 75 clinical studies including the Lancet-published TALENT trial.
Strong R&D with 119 patents granted, 78 pending and R&D spend of about 8.6% of FY26 revenue.
Integrated manufacturing in India and Thailand, with large spare capacity (stent utilisation 78% in FY26).
Improving profitability: PAT swung from a Rs 7 crore loss in FY24 to Rs 69 crore profit in FY26; EBITDA margin up to 14.1%.
Falling distributor concentration: top 10 distributors dropped from 26% of revenue in FY24 to 16% in FY26.
Proven acquisition playbook (Imex Spain, Zarek Brazil, Vascular Concepts, Vascular Innovations) and institutional investor backing.

risks.title: High receivables and rising bad debts
risks.detail: Trade receivables were Rs 306.56 crore at June 2026 (76 days of sales); bad debts jumped to Rs 18.56 crore in FY26 from Rs 2.95 crore in FY25. Long credit is extended to distributors.

risks.title: Heavy borrowings and covenant breaches
risks.detail: Borrowings were Rs 320.63 crore at June 2026 (Rs 269.53 crore at March 2026), mostly short-term. The company has breached financial covenants in the past, and a subsidiary breached a term loan covenant in FY26 (waived by lender).

risks.title: Extensive regulatory and certification dependence
risks.detail: Products are Class III devices needing CE and Indian approvals. Many CE certificates under the old MDD expire December 31, 2027 and must move to the stricter EU MDR; only Supraflex Cruz has MDR certification so far.

risks.title: Pure offer for sale, no money to the company
risks.detail: The whole offer is 13,822,116 shares sold by existing investors (13.60% of pre-offer capital); the company receives nothing, so no funds go to debt reduction or growth.

risks.title: Weak debt service coverage
risks.detail: Debt service coverage ratio was only 0.65 in FY26, 0.47 in FY25 and 0.12 in the June 2026 quarter, while interest coverage was 4.29 in FY26.

risks.title: Pending litigation and tax disputes
risks.detail: 98 tax proceedings and 2 criminal cases against the company, with quantifiable amount of Rs 131.97 crore; Directors face Rs 24.85 crore and Promoters Rs 6.10 crore.

risks.title: International operations risk
risks.detail: About 74% of FY26 revenue is outside India (Europe 38.66%, rest of world 35.21%), exposing results to currency, tariff, regulatory and tender risks across 77 countries.

risks.title: Untraceable historical corporate records
risks.detail: Several RoC filings and challans for share allotments since 2001 (items up to 13.68% of pre-offer capital) could not be located, which could invite regulatory action.

notes: FY24-FY26 restated consolidated, Rs crore (converted from INR million); June 2026 quarter stub ignored (revenue Rs 351.67 crore, PAT Rs 15.09 crore). net_worth and reserves are attributable to owners (excl. NCI). borrowings = current plus non-current (matches RHP). cash_and_bank = cash equivalents plus other bank balances. debt_equity is the RHP total borrowings/total equity; current_ratio computed from the balance sheet; weighted_avg_eps is diluted. Price band, issue size, P/E and post-issue shares are blank in the RHP. Balance sheet was reconstructed from garbled text and cross-checked to totals. Reservation percentages are SEBI limits (QIB up to 50%, anchor up to 60% of QIB, NII at least 15%, retail at least 35%); employee reservation is up to 250,000 shares.
